_note: PACING PROFILES — the timing of a spoken lesson, as data. A spoken scene is a sequence of engineered silences as much as it is a sequence of lines, and those silences are a TEACHING decision (how long an orienting sentence gets to be read, how long the learner gets to think before the character helps). So they live server-side, named, and are dialed per lesson rather than hardcoded in the renderer. A dialogue picks a profile by id; a node may override a single value where one beat genuinely needs it.
_axis: Profiles are ordered by how much room the learner is given. `onboarding` is the most generous. Later lessons withdraw scaffolding by moving to a tighter profile — no renderer change, no re-authoring.
_frameTiming: An on-ramp line dwells for `frameLineMs` PLUS `frameCharMs` per character, because a 45-character line and a 73-character line do not take the same time to read. Lines accumulate rather than replacing each other, so the learner can still be reading line 1 when line 3 arrives.
_beatTiming: A beat the character carries himself through (no turn asked) holds for beatHoldMs PLUS beatCharMs per character of the longest text on screen, then its caption is replaced. It is the only caption the learner cannot go back to: on a hand-over beat the line recedes but stays up beside their prompt.

guided.label: Guided — the learner knows the format, still gets the slow re-speak

brisk.label: Brisk — scaffolds mostly withdrawn, silence carries more
